To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) His78 is the site of phosphorylation of the phosphocarrier enzyme IIIlac, (2) the phosphorylation of enzyme IIIlac occurs at the histidine ring nitrogen, (3) the role of the histidine residue His82 is to facilitate the phosphotransfers to and from enzyme IIIlac, and (4) the histidine ring nitrogens in enzyme IIIlac do not play a major role in the conformation of the protein, as indicated by the similarity
the histidine residues of lactose-specific Enzyme III are involved in the phosphotransfers and that the histidine residue His78 is the phosphorylation site for lactose-specific Enzyne III.

His82 is not the active-site for the phosphorylation of enzyme III, but it is the site of the phosphorylated peptide that was identified in the previous studies by the cleavage of 32P-labelled enzyme III.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the mechanism of phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of the phosphocarrier enzyme IIIlac.
the characterization of the lactose-specific phospho-carrier protein of the phosphoenolpy-ruvate-dependent system in Staphylococci and with the elucidation of the active-site structure.
the elucidation of the role of His78 and His82 for the phosphotransfers catalyzed by lactose-specific enzyme I and lactose-specific enzyme HI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
His78 is essential for the phosphorylation of lactoserice enzyme III, whereas His82 is essential for a high rate and efficiency of phosphotransfer.
the active-site of the phosphocarrier proteins of the bacterial phosphotransfer system is the imidazole ring of a histidine residue, which is not necessarily the N-terminal residue of the protein.

the active-site for the phospho-HPr:enzyme III phosphotransfer is located at the N-terminus of lactose-specific protein III, whereas the C-terminal region is important for the enzyme II:enzyme III phospho-transfer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phosphoenolpyrruvate-dependent phosphotransterase system of Stapylococcus aureus is a highly regulated system, in which the phosphorylation of lactos-specific enzyme III by the phosphoenol-pyruric acid-dependent phosphotransferring protein HPr (histidine containing protein) is the rate-limiting step.

the active-site of lactose-specific phospho-carrier protein enzyme III for phosphorylation is His78, while His82 is the residue that enhances the efficiency and velocity of phosphotransfer to the lactose-specific enzyme IIA.
His78 is essential for the phosphorylation of enzyme III and the role of His82 in the system is to enhance the velocity of the reaction by stabilizing the phospho-intermediate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active site for phosphorylation is not necessarily the site of phospho group transfer.
the NMR spectroscopy is a useful technique for the study of the structure and dynamics of phosphoenolpyrurate-dependent phosphotransfase system proteins.
NMR spectroscopy is a valuable tool in determining the role of amino acid side chains in the conformational changes that occur upon ligand binding and phosphorylation.
